name: Saint Vitus
label: SST
lede: A Black Sabbath worship band too slow for L.A. metal, signed by Black Flag, pelted by punks, and still playing doom after four singers and forty-odd years.

eras.title: Too slow for L.A. metal
eras.text: In a Los Angeles metal scene racing toward speed and hairspray, a band playing Black Sabbath at half speed had nowhere to go. The punks, and Greg Ginn's label, turned out to be the only people who would have them.

years.h: Tyrant forms in Los Angeles, and fires its singer after one show
years.p: Guitarist [[Dave Chandler|dbcf34bc-9a5a-45ea-a586-d7c2fc64d114]], bassist [[Mark Adams|0c222999-72fa-4fb7-9205-eede45ce030d]] and drummer [[Armando Acosta|439b0bb5-df9e-4484-927f-292ce784f6cb]] start out as Tyrant. The first singer is gone after the first show and [[Scott Reagers|bb347751-07fa-4acd-925e-4b5b911caff5]] takes over.
years.xp: Their touchstones were Black Sabbath, Judas Priest, Blue Cheer, Blue Öyster Cult and Alice Cooper, all played slower and heavier than the models.

years.h: Tyrant becomes Saint Vitus, after a Black Sabbath song
years.p: The band renames itself after Sabbath's St. Vitus Dance. Dave Chandler later told Louder the metal people hated them, so they ended up in the punk scene.

years.cap: Saint Vitus in Los Angeles, early 1980s
years.h: [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] show up at a Saint Vitus gig and offer a deal
years.p: SST people come to flyer the parking lot for their crossover band Overkill. Dave Chandler asks if Black Flag will come; [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]], [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]] and [[Chuck Dukowski|19a07153-933f-4725-a5de-477cb3554517]] do, and ask Saint Vitus to record that night.
years.xp: Chandler told Westword the answer was immediate. Ginn signed them, Chandler said, because they were the complete opposite of what was popular in metal.

eras.title: Thrown at the punks' feet
eras.text: SST put a long-haired doom band on tour with Black Flag, Saccharine Trust and the rest of its hardcore roster. The crowds threw everything they could find. Saint Vitus kept coming back until the crowds changed their minds.

years.h: Saint Vitus, the SST debut
years.p: Scott Reagers sings, Dave Chandler's guitar crawls, and a punk label releases one of the first American doom records.

years.big: Doom in front of hardcore kids. Everything not nailed down came flying.
q: They threw us at the punks' feet.
years.h: First tour with Black Flag: nearly every punk hates Saint Vitus
years.p: On Saint Vitus' first cross-country tour with Black Flag, Dave Chandler says about ninety percent of the punks hated them and threw whatever wasn't nailed down.
years.xp:
SST's plan was blunt. Chandler told Louder the label simply threw Saint Vitus at the punks, and that taking the abuse and returning is what won them over.

They also toured with [[The Brood|2ef8706e-baea-4c56-abec-91fbd70a303d]], [[Saccharine Trust|0bd450a7-32dd-496f-a0d4-1f71a2226add]], the Mentors, Napalm Beach and DC3.

years.h: Hallow's Victim, Scott Reagers' second Saint Vitus album
years.p: The second SST album, followed the same year by The Walking Dead EP, the last Saint Vitus records with Reagers for a decade.

years.h: Saint Vitus go back out to the punks, and spit back
years.p: On the August 1985 return tour the crowds start to turn. Dave Chandler told Westword the punks spat at them, the band spat back, and the punks decided Saint Vitus were cool.

eras.title: Wino from Maryland
eras.text: The singer who defined Saint Vitus came from the D.C. suburbs: Scott "Wino" Weinrich of The Obsessed, met on tour and hired after one night. With him Saint Vitus made Born Too Late, the record doom bands still measure themselves against.

years.h: Scott Reagers leaves Saint Vitus in the middle of a tour
years.p: Saint Vitus' original singer, Scott Reagers, departs early in 1986.

years.h: [[Scott Weinrich|141b095c-a290-478e-a6ae-b1d3f7899835]], aka Wino, joins Saint Vitus after one night
years.p: A friend had mailed Saint Vitus a tape of Maryland's [[The Obsessed|aa043c18-c0a0-4cbe-bda0-8541f1fe59bd]]. They met its singer, Scott "Wino" Weinrich, on a 1986 D.C.-area tour, talked for one night, and he became their singer.
years.xp:
Dave Chandler told Westword that early on they accidentally left Wino at a highway rest stop. He still lent them twenty dollars for gas.

Wino wrote Bitter Truth, Looking Glass and Ice Monkey, which Down later covered.

years.h: Born Too Late, the doom metal anthem
years.p: Recorded at Total Access in Redondo Beach with SST's [[Joe Carducci|6f08ef70-2da6-4575-8ec2-22438145f5d2]], Wino's first Saint Vitus album is widely called the band's masterpiece. The title track is about being out of step with every scene around them.

years.h: Thirsty and Miserable: Saint Vitus cover Black Flag
years.p: A thank-you to the band that got them signed: an EP led by Saint Vitus' slowed-down take on Black Flag's Thirsty and Miserable.

years.h: Mournful Cries, Saint Vitus' last SST studio album
years.p: The second album with Wino. By 1989 Saint Vitus has left SST for Hellhound Records.

years.h: V on Hellhound, with Wino's Ice Monkey
years.p: Saint Vitus' fifth album and the first on Germany's Hellhound, whose European doom audience was bigger than anything the band had at home.

years.h: Wino quits to bring back [[The Obsessed|aa043c18-c0a0-4cbe-bda0-8541f1fe59bd]]
years.p: When Hellhound releases an Obsessed retrospective, Scott "Wino" Weinrich leaves Saint Vitus to re-form his old band.

eras.title: A Swede, Don Dokken, and the last rites
eras.text: Without Wino, Saint Vitus turned to a Swedish singer and, improbably, a hair-metal star behind the desk. Then Scott Reagers came home for one last album before the band called it off.

years.h: C.O.D., produced by Don Dokken
years.p: Former Count Raven singer Christian "Chritus" Linderson fronts Saint Vitus, and the producer is Don Dokken. Linderson tours Europe and America with them until 1993.

years.h: Scott Reagers returns for Die Healing
years.p: Saint Vitus' original singer is back for the album Dave Chandler considered the band's finest. After the tour, Saint Vitus breaks up in 1996.

eras.title: Kids at Wacken knew the words
eras.text: A festival crowd half Dave Chandler's age singing his old songs convinced him to call the others. The classic lineup came back for one Chicago night, then for good, and lost its drummer along the way.

years.h: At Wacken, young fans sing Saint Vitus songs back to Dave Chandler
years.p: Playing Wacken Open Air with his band Debris Inc., Dave Chandler hears young fans singing Saint Vitus lyrics and wants the others to see it.

years.h: The Born Too Late lineup reunites at Chicago's Double Door
years.p: Wino, Dave Chandler, Mark Adams and Armando Acosta play together for the first time since 1991, a one-off in Chicago.

years.h: Saint Vitus reunite for good with Wino
years.p: The same classic lineup starts touring again.

years.h: Armando Acosta leaves after 30 years; Henry Vasquez takes over
years.p: Health problems force Armando Acosta out before the 2009 European tour ends. Henry Vasquez of Blood of the Sun becomes the drummer.

years.h: Armando Acosta dies at 58
years.p: Saint Vitus' drummer since 1978 died of arterial complications, according to Wikipedia, and was buried at Riverside National Cemetery in California.

eras.title: Lillie, a Norwegian cell, and the long goodbye
eras.text: Saint Vitus' first album in seventeen years was named after the pills Dave Chandler took as a kid. Then its singer was deported, the original singer came back again, and the founding bassist fell ill.

years.h: Lillie: F-65, named for a barbiturate
years.p: Signed to Season of Mist, Saint Vitus releases its first studio album since 1995 and first with Wino since 1990. Louder says the title refers to Dave Chandler's childhood barbiturate addiction.

q: I take full responsibility for the consequences of my actions.
years.h: Wino is arrested in Norway with 11 grams of meth and deported
years.p: On tour in Norway, Scott "Wino" Weinrich is arrested for possessing 11 grams of methamphetamine. He is deported on November 11 and misses the tour's last six dates.
years.xp:
According to The Local, he was held three days in solitary, given a 16-day sentence, and barred from staying in Scandinavia or the EU. Saint Vitus finished the European dates without him.

Wino apologized publicly to Norway.

years.h: Scott Reagers back in Saint Vitus after 20 years
years.p: Scott Reagers sings a U.S. date in Austin and a European tour, and rejoins permanently.

years.h: Pat Bruders fills in for an ailing Mark Adams
years.p: On the U.S. tour with The Skull and Witch Mountain, Pat Bruders of [[Crowbar|04fc15f9-2555-4699-9215-2ee6c84a2346]] and Down plays bass for Mark Adams, who has health problems. Bruders stays.

years.h: A second self-titled album, with Scott Reagers singing
years.p: Saint Vitus names its ninth studio album after itself, 35 years after the first. Reagers, Dave Chandler, Pat Bruders and Henry Vasquez play on it.

years.h: Mark Adams dies at 64
years.p: The founding bassist, off the road since 2016 and revealed in 2018 to have Parkinson's disease, died of complications from it. He played on every Saint Vitus album until 2012.
